drawn.readLog: ACC-T07R at ?tab=meters&meter=e-4417&view=reads — head 'Read log — E-4417', group THE METER (Meter · Service · Meter type · Read method · Installed · Multiplier · Status · Reads held 24, newest first), table THE READS (DATE ▼ · CHANNEL · READING · USAGE · EXPORT · HOW IT WAS COLLECTED · STATUS), footer 'Read from the meter's own record · Export the log · Close'
rules: Read log opens that one meter's reads over this unit without leaving the tab. It is a row action rather than a table per meter, because a unit with six meters would otherwise push the list itself off the screen.
The meters belong to the unit, not to the account — they stay when the occupant leaves. The services this account holds are a separate fact and live in the Service group on Overview.
Two of the columns look alike and are not: meter type is what the meter IS, read method is how the reading is COLLECTED.

elsewhere.⇩ Export (both tables): not rendered — POST /exports registers neither a meter list nor a read log, and BR-SHL-010 keeps an undeclared capability unrendered rather than wired to a 404 (hard-won law 2). The same sentence AccountDocumentsTab and DisconnectsTab already make.
elsewhere.The read log as a MODAL: opens OVER the tab as an addressable panel at ?meter=<id> instead. It holds a table of its own and the drawing gives it its own address, which is the modal-or-screen test's own answer, and it is WorkOrderPanel's existing shape one module over (B14 rule 38 — the UI rules own how a thing is built).
elsewhere.Sort: Meter # ▼ as a control: the sort IS meter number and it is the only one offered, so no header is pressable — a control with one option is not a control. The order is compareMeters, numeric-aware so M-999 precedes M-4021.
